elements.name: Patient
elements.doc: Demographics and other administrative information about an individual or animal receiving care or other health-related services.

elements.name: identifier
elements.doc: An identifier for this patient.

elements.name: active
elements.doc: Whether this patient record is in active use. Many systems use this property to mark as non-current patients, such as those that have not been seen for a period of time based on an organization's business rules. It is often used to filter patient lists to exclude inactive patients Deceased patients may also be marked as inactive for the same reasons, but may be active for some time after death.

elements.name: name
elements.doc: A name associated with the individual.

elements.name: telecom
elements.doc: A contact detail (e.g. a telephone number or an email address) by which the individual may be contacted.

elements.name: gender
elements.doc: Administrative Gender - the gender that the patient is considered to have for administration and record keeping purposes.

elements.name: birthDate
elements.doc: The date of birth for the individual.

elements.name: address
elements.doc: An address for the individual.

elements.name: maritalStatus
elements.doc: This field contains a patient's most recent marital (civil) status.

elements.name: photo
elements.doc: Image of the patient.

elements.name: contact
elements.doc: A contact party (e.g. guardian, partner, friend) for the patient.

elements.name: relationship
elements.doc: The nature of the relationship between the patient and the contact person.

elements.name: organization
elements.doc: Organization on behalf of which the contact is acting or for which the contact is working.

elements.name: period
elements.doc: The period during which this contact person or organization is valid to be contacted relating to this patient.

elements.name: communication
elements.doc: A language which may be used to communicate with the patient about his or her health.

elements.name: language
elements.doc: The ISO-639-1 alpha 2 code in lower case for the language, optionally followed by a hyphen and the ISO-3166-1 alpha 2 code for the region in upper case; e.g. "en" for English, or "en-US" for American English versus "en-EN" for England English.

elements.name: preferred
elements.doc: Indicates whether or not the patient prefers this language (over other languages he masters up a certain level).

elements.name: generalPractitioner
elements.doc: Patient's nominated care provider.

elements.name: managingOrganization
elements.doc: Organization that is the custodian of the patient record.

elements.name: link
elements.doc: Link to another patient resource that concerns the same actual patient.

elements.name: other
elements.doc: The other patient resource that the link refers to.

elements.name: type
elements.doc: The type of link between this patient resource and another patient resource.
